newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Pasminco sees ready markets for lead.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Pasminco sees ready markets for lead.

text.p: Base metals producer Pasminco Ltd said on Thursday it had ready export markets for increased production from its BHAS smelter at Port Pirie in South Australia which would also assist to cut unit production costs.
Pasminco executive general manager, metals, John Winckel, told a news conference the company had plans to reduce unit production costs at Port Pirie by 12 percent by 1997/98.

A A$33 million upgrade at Port Pirie to increase annual lead production to 250,000 tonnes from 200,000 tonnes and silver production to 450 tonnes from 220 tonnes announced earlier on Thursday would be part of that programme, he said.
Winckel said 90 percent of lead produced at Port Pirie was sold to Asian markets, and the company had ready markets for the increased production.
He said the upgrade would mean Port Pirie could refine all of the current 36,000 tonnes of unrefined lead bullion produced a year at Pasminco's sulphide smelter in Boolaroo, New South Wales.

Currently only 10,000 tonnes of bullion is refined at Port Pirie, with the remainder sold to a South Korean plant for refining and eventual sale into Asian markets in competition with Pasminco, he said.
"Following the upgrade, the Port Pirie smelter will be able to process all of the sulphide bullion, thereby allowing Pasminco to capture a larger share of the Asian lead market," he said.

Winckel said replacement of the continuous desilverising process with batch processing would allow BHAS to treat lead concentrates from The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd's new Cannington Mine in north Queensland.
"Basically what we are doing over time is planning out the diminishing resources at Broken Hill and planning in Cannington and other feed sources," he said.
Input from Cannington would be about 20,000 tonnes in the next two years, he said.
